annotations.annotation_text: Page 567 opens Book 3, Chapter 4 ("The Bedroom Scene") during the Age of Men (closing) phase. This passage continues HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream, featuring HCE, ALP, Shem, Shaun, Issy. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "broken" on page 567 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men (closing) phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 567 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men (closing) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
